The dog I brought to your clinic was not my pet he was a building stray dog who needed urgent medical attention. I stepped forward to help him because no one else did, and I believed that as a vet, you would understand your responsibility to treat an animal in pain.

Since he was a street dog, I didn’t know exactly how to carry or handle him safely that’s why I requested your staff to help lift him onto the table. Instead, you twisted it as if I didn’t want to touch “my own dog,” which is completely false and shameful.

You said you were busy treating other animals the truth is, you preferred to attend to healthy dogs first while ignoring a paralyzed stray who was suffering and needed immediate help. That clearly shows how selective and careless your priorities are.

And yes, you did say that you won’t take any responsibility if something happens to the dog during treatment. That’s not professionalism that’s fear and avoidance. A real vet gives confidence and tries to save the animal, not push it away. Your own words made it clear that you didn’t want to take the risk, and that’s exactly why I refused that condition because you weren’t ready to stand by your duty as a doctor.

You talk about honesty and accuse others of false allegations, but we are not even personally known to each other. I have no reason to hold grudges. What I am writing is the truth what I saw, what you said, and how you behaved. I’m only exposing this to make the Mira-Bhayandar public aware of the heartless way your clinic treats strays and the people who try to help them.

You say I didn’t pay any fees money is not the issue here. Compassion and humanity are. A vet’s duty doesn’t end where money stops. But your arrogance, harsh words, and insults like “no brain” and “no common sense” show you’ve lost all respect for the people who try to save lives.

And most importantly that innocent dog is no more with us now. He passed away, and yes, you are also responsible for that. If you had treated him on time instead of arguing and refusing, his life could have been saved. That’s something your clinic can never deny or erase.

You said I have no brain, but it’s clear that you have no heart. A person who insults others, avoids responsibility, and refuses to help a dying animal doesn’t deserve to be called a vet. What happened to that stray will always speak louder than any of your excuses and the truth will reach everyone.

I strongly urge the management to reflect on their practices and take immediate action to prioritize animal welfare over profit. This clinic is not a place for responsible or compassionate pet care.
